project_tracker_diagnostic: Subevergreen; narrow leathery leaves with densely pale/whitish lower surfaces; deep goblet/funnel acorn cup; spindle-shaped acute acorn; can form clonal mottes.
verified_target_counties: Hays; Travis; Blanco; Burnet; Comal; Gillespie; Kerr; Bandera; Edwards; Real; Uvalde; Williamson; Bell; Kendall; Medina; Tom Green; Val Verde

morphology_keys.habit: Tree or shrub; often subevergreen; shrubby plants may form large clonal stands.
morphology_keys.bark: Dark brown to black and scaly.
morphology_keys.leaves: Oblong-elliptic to narrowly ovate/lanceolate; margins entire or with a few teeth and often minutely revolute; lower surface pale/whitish from dense appressed stellate hairs.
morphology_keys.acorn: Nut dark brown, often longitudinally striped, subfusiform and acute to narrowly barrel-shaped; cup funnel-, hemispheric-, or deeply goblet-shaped.

photo_strategy.oak_specific_tightening: Prioritize multi-photo late-summer/fall observations to increase the chance of mature leaves and acorns, plus curated taxon reference photos.

look_here_first: Start with mature acorn shape plus the scaly cup: Texas live oak often has a narrow, noticeably pointed/spindle-like nut ~20–30 mm long seated in a relatively deep funnel/goblet cup. Combine this with pale appressed-stellate leaf undersides and central Texas limestone habitat; leaf shape or evergreen habit alone is insufficient.

best_tie_breakers: FNA strict fusiformis acorn usually narrow and apically acute, typically 20–30 mm long; strict virginiana nut more often rounded/blunt apically, typically 15–20 mm long (overlap at extremes).
Both can have deep cupules (8–15 mm high) and pale appressed-stellate lower leaf hairs; these are NOT exclusive to one species.

Geographic provenance is supporting evidence: escarpment/Edwards Plateau limestone stands favor fusiformis; coastal-plain native stands favor virginiana, but cultivated/older broad-name live oak records are not definitive.
unreliable_alone: A planted Central Texas nursery 'live oak' tag.
diagnostic_comparison.taxon_concept_guardrail: Retain strict Q. virginiana county-native assessment unresolved; different floras may include fusiformis as a variety. Hybrid/introgressed individuals exist.
diagnostic_comparison.acorn_guardrail: Both live-oak taxa may show pointed green developing acorns. The elongated two-tone mature Q fusiformis nuts are a helpful group-level cue but not a standalone proof; without cups, ruler and provenance do not force ID.
